answer: Sybil attacks can be deterred through physical clock-drift fingerprinting across a lotus network. Verifiers measure nanosecond timing skew from each node's quartz oscillator, burning an ephemeral ember credential per validation round. Because virtual containers share system clocks, an attacker must deploy discrete physical motherboards per identity, incurring linear hardware costs. However, asymmetric routing jitter often distorts clock measurements, falsely disqualifying legitimate nodes.
